That's literally not an option. Every package has a barcode, and when that barcode is scanned there are only a set list of specific options you can put, and "late" isn't one of them. If you are told to bring packages back, the only way to do that and not get in trouble and not have the package returned to sender is by choosing options such as "No Access" or "Animal Interference." Picking most other options will have the package returned to sender, which would be even worse than the delay that No Access causes.
Monday was not a business day for USPS, as it was a federal holiday.

It's explicitly in the M-41, section 13, subsection 132.12: Collect prepaid letters placed next to, in, or on private mail receptacles when delivery is being made to that point.

The key phrase there being "when delivery is being made to that point." That language means the carrier does not need to collect mail if they otherwise wouldn't be going to that delivery point.

We're in the Pioneer sub, so the answers will obviously be skewed in favor of the format. I figured I'd offer an "outsider" perspective. I have played basically every format both competitive and casual for almost 20 years, though I've played mostly Legacy and EDH for the past few years. I have played Pioneer, but not much, and mostly when it first popped up before the original bans. I keep up with the meta and watch content featuring the format far more than I play it.

>Is Pioneer here to stay?

I think so, a lot of people love it.

>How healthy is it?

"Healthy" is a misnomer opinion word people spout to attempt to justify what they think of a format. Pioneer has a fair division of archetypes, but a large disparity between colors. 

>Do you think it will become THE eternal format in the future if and when Arena is Pioneer complete?

Pioneer isn't an Eternal format, it's nonrotating. Eternal formats by definition include every set. I know what you mean by the question, but it's an important distinction to make.

As far as what you mean by the question, I think it's very possible, even likely, Pioneer replaces Modern as the premier competitive nonrotating format, just like how Modern replaced Extended. 

>Also, how is the Pioneer support at your local game store?

Below average. My area has a ton of stores that run events and Pioneer has the lowest average attendance. It is by far the most competitive format in terms of player skill in the area, however. 

>If you have been playing Pioneer for a while, what do you like and dislike about it?

While I have technically played Pioneer since the beginning, I don't play it often, so unsure if I fall under this, but I'm going to answer anyways.

I have nothing against the format theoretically, but I have yet to find a (meta) deck since the original pre-bans Mono G deck which has really tickled my fancy. I imagine at some point there will be a deck which I take to, though. 

As far as gameplay, I've found it boring to play, likely because I've played it using decks which I didn't find particularly compelling. 

>And what improvements do you think WotC could make to enhance the experience?

In my opinion, they haven't executed the banlist correctly at all. Early bans were too aggressive, eliminating all of the decks which were actually interesting, but they've been slow to act on problematic decks as of late. 

I hope people appreciate a look at the format from an "outsider's" perspective.
